title: Procurement rules for service contracts and Progressive Wage Mark compliance
asked: Ms Yeo Wan Ling asked whether public sector procurement frameworks for service contracts such as catering will be reviewed so that factors beyond price, including Progressive Wage Model compliance and service quality, get meaningful weightage, and whether public sector buyers will adopt outcome-based contracts with periodic price reviews and longer terms to support sustainable wage and productivity investments.
response: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong said the Government uses a comprehensive set of criteria combining price and quality in procurement evaluations, and that some sectors require eligible suppliers to hold Progressive Wage Mark certification. Central guidance tells procuring entities to adopt outcome-based contracts where appropriate, as in cleaning and facilities management. For multi-year contracts, tenderers can submit prices for each contract year rather than one fixed price, so they can account for wage adjustments and productivity investments. He added that PW Mark contractors must maintain certification and notify authorities of changes, and that agencies can terminate contracts for non-compliance.

key_points.point: Government procurement evaluations combine price and quality considerations.
key_points.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
key_points.quote: The Government uses a comprehensive set of criteria, combining price and quality considerations in procurement evaluations.

key_points.point: In some sectors, eligible Government suppliers must have Progressive Wage Mark certification.
key_points.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
key_points.quote: eligible Government suppliers must have the Progressive Wage Mark (PWM) certification.

key_points.point: Central guidance has been given to all Government procuring entities to adopt outcome-based contracts where appropriate and feasible.
key_points.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
key_points.quote: Central guidance has been provided to all Government procuring entities to adopt outcome-based contracts where appropriate and feasible

key_points.point: Examples of outcome-based contracts are in cleaning services and facilities management services.
key_points.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
key_points.quote: Examples of this are in the procurement of cleaning services and facilities management services.

key_points.point: For multi-year contracts, tenderers can typically submit prices for each contract year rather than a single fixed price over the entire duration.
key_points.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
key_points.quote: tenderers are typically able to submit prices for each contract year, rather than a single fixed price over the entire duration.

key_points.point: This allows tenderers to account for wage adjustments and productivity investments over time in their pricing.
key_points.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
key_points.quote: This allows tenderers to account for wage adjustments and productivity investments over time in their pricing.

key_points.point: Contractors who are PW Mark eligible must obtain and maintain the PW Mark throughout the contract period.
key_points.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
key_points.quote: Contractors who are PW Mark eligible are required to obtain and maintain the PW Mark throughout the contract period.

key_points.point: Contractors must notify contracting authorities of any changes to their PW Mark status.
key_points.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
key_points.quote: They are also required to notify the contracting authorities if there are any changes to their PW Mark status.

key_points.point: Government agencies reserve the right to take necessary action, including terminating the contract, if contractors fail to comply with requirements.
key_points.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
key_points.quote: we reserve the right to take necessary action if contractors fail to comply with the requirements, including the right to terminate the contract.

key_points.point: Where there are further updates to PW Mark requirements, the Ministry of Finance will review its guidance to agencies accordingly, where necessary.
key_points.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong
key_points.quote: Where there are further updates to the PW Mark requirements, the Ministry of Finance will review our guidance to agencies accordingly, where necessary.
